candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Astronomical Book (1 Enoch 72-82) (c. 250 BC)

The angels who escort Enoch tell him: 'Declare everything to thy son Methuselah, and show to all thy children that no flesh is righteous in the sight of the Lord, for He is their Creator' — the foundational anthropological pessimism that anticipates Pauline 'all have sinned' (Rom 3:23). The Tewahedo reading connects this verse to the Romans passage explicitly: the apostolic doctrine of universal sinfulness has its Jewish-canonical basis in the Mäṣḥafä Hēnok, not introduced by Paul ex nihilo but inherited from the prophetic-apocalyptic tradition. The pessimism is grounded ontologically ('for He is their Creator' — only the Creator is finally righteous) rather than merely empirically.
